text:
leah (AE): Heads-up: HarborLedger wants a technical POC to move from RivalAI -> Redwood. Their blockers: response shape (they rely on Rival's trailing metadata fields), streaming chunk semantics, and an infosec questionnaire + network diagram. Can SE/Eng scope?
omar (SE): Yep. First ask: can they share 30 representative prompts + 10 streaming sessions? we'll run them through both systems. Also want to know if Rival is doing any post-generation canonicalization (e.g., trimming, regex fixes).
leah (AE): They'll send prompts tomorrow AM. They stressed minimal client changes — want an adapter/proxy that looks like Rival to their app.
dina (Eng): That's doable. Plan: shadow proxy that forwards requests to both Rival and Redwood, records candidate outputs and tokens, and optionally returns Rival output while we iterate. For streaming, we'll need to emulate Rival's chunk envelope fields (chunk_id, partial=true, final=false).
marco (Solutions): I'll assemble a scoring matrix. Metrics: token_delta_percent, sbert_similarity, normalized_edit_distance, streaming_chunk_alignment (%), and a route-level parity_score.
omar (SE): Important: they rely on Rival's extra metadata fields: "source_span" and "confidence_vector" appended to JSON output. We'll either re-add placeholder fields or try to compute equivalents. If we fabricate fields, legal needs to sign off on accuracy claims.
sec-bot: Uploaded: HarborLedger_SecPacket_2026.pdf to /shared/sales/harbor/ (link: https://files.redwood/harbor/packet_2026.pdf) :white_check_mark:
dina (Eng): Prototype steps: 1) simple reverse-proxy that duplicates requests -> both endpoints; 2) store Rival response + Redwood response; 3) scoring job runs nightly; 4) optional post-process layer that maps Redwood shape -> Rival shape. I can have a quick prototype container in 24-36h.
marco (Solutions): Example quick harness (local):
```bash
# run batch through both endpoints
for f in samples/*.json; do
  curl -s -X POST https://rival.company/api/generate -d @"$f" > rival.json
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @"$f" > redwood.json
  python tools/score.py rival.json redwood.json >> scores.csv
done
```
marco (Solutions): Score fields: prompt_id, route, rival_tokens, redwood_tokens, sbert_sim, edit_dist, streaming_mismatch_count
omar (SE): Also run a quick policy diff: Rival's profanity/evasion filter settings might remove or alter outputs. If HarborLedger relies on that filtering, parity might be impossible without policy alignment. Call that out in scope.
leah (AE): Pricing question: HarborLedger asked for an estimate of incremental cost for parity work during POC (shadowing + normalization). Any ballpark?
dina (Eng): Ballpark: running duplicate requests during POC increases token bill roughly 1.0x (i.e., double) for generation plus small compute for scoring. If we add normalization passes (post-process loops), expect +10-30% extra compute on top for heavy rules.
omar (SE): If we need to fine-tune an internal Redwood model to match outputs, that's a separate scope and cost. We'll present that as option C.
leah (AE): Fallback strategy: can we route specific API routes back to Rival automatically if parity drops below threshold?
dina (Eng): Yes — traffic-split + per-route health checks. We'll maintain per-route parity metrics and a kill-switch. Legal needs to review dual-routing clause.
marco (Solutions): Proposed timeline (fast POC): day 0 collect prompts + streaming captures + sec form; day 1-2 deploy shadow proxy + ingest 5k samples; day 3 analyze & run remediation rules; day 4 produce parity report + recommended adapter rules; day 5 demo & discuss next steps (fine-tune or production adapter).
omar (SE): Action items: - leah: collect prompt samples + Rival API contract (EOD tomorrow) - marco: scaffold scoring harness & template report - dina: prototype proxy shim & incompatibility doc - sec-bot: confirm sec packet in shared folder
leah (AE): I'll chase HarborLedger for the bundle. Keeping all updates in this thread. Any other concerns?
marco (Solutions): Flag: if they use Rival's fine-tuned private models with non-public special tokens, mapping may need token remapping rules. We'll flag as medium risk.
omar (SE): And if streaming finalization markers differ (Rival uses "is_final": true only on final chunk), we must ensure we don't emit partial finalizations prematurely — could break client logic.
dina (Eng): Good point. We'll include streaming emulation tests in the harness.
leah (AE): Great — thanks team. I'll post the prompt bundle here when received. :rocket:
